title: sync --push sends code-lane work as a merge request
goal: kbgit.py sync --push sends a content-only range to the integration remote's main as today; a range with any code-lane commit (its content commits ride along) is rebased on the integration main, gated and pushed as branch code/<id> (the first KB-Work id in the range, else HEAD's short hash) with the push options merge_request.create, merge_request.target=<branch>, merge_request.auto_merge and merge_request.remove_source_branch; when the remote answers that it does not support push options, sync pushes the same branch without them and prints that a merge or pull request must be opened from it; it exits 0 once the branch is pushed and never moves main; pipelines of code/* branches run the gate jobs without a click; tests.py -k TestCodeLaneSync proves both push paths against local bare remotes, and -k TestCiCodeBranch the CI rule

gates.question: May sync --push push code/<id> branches (not main) to the integration remote and open merge requests there?
options: yes, code/<id> branches with auto-merge; the branch is deleted on merge
yes, but without auto-merge: a person merges
no: code stays on direct push
gates.recommendation: yes, code/<id> branches with auto-merge; the branch is deleted on merge
gates.answer: yes, code/<id> branches with auto-merge; the branch is deleted on merge

gates.question: Every job in .gitlab-ci.yml is manual with allow_failure: true, and an optional manual job never counts toward a pipeline's status (automated-merge-requests.md:34), so auto-merge on a code/<id> merge request would wait on, or pass, a pipeline in which no test ran. Which jobs run without a click in pipelines of code/* branches?
options: kb-tests and kb-trailers run automatically on code/* branches; every other job stays manual
every job runs automatically on code/* branches
every job stays manual: a person starts kb-tests on each merge request before auto-merge can merge
gates.recommendation: kb-tests and kb-trailers run automatically on code/* branches; every other job stays manual
gates.answer: kb-tests and kb-trailers run automatically on code/* branches; every other job stays manual

gates.question: sync finds code/<id> already on the integration remote (an open merge request) after the work changed or main moved, so the rebased branch is not a fast-forward of it; kb/_self/git.md says never git push --force. What does sync do?
options: push the rebased branch with --force-with-lease against the fetched tip, to code/* branches only, and send merge_request.auto_merge again (new commits on a merge request cancel auto-merge, automated-merge-requests.md:24)
push to a new branch code/<id>-<n> and leave the old merge request for a person to close
refuse with exit 2 naming the open merge request
gates.recommendation: push the rebased branch with --force-with-lease against the fetched tip, to code/* branches only, and send merge_request.auto_merge again (new commits on a merge request cancel auto-merge, automated-merge-requests.md:24)
gates.answer: push the rebased branch with --force-with-lease against the fetched tip, to code/* branches only, and send merge_request.auto_merge again (new commits on a merge request cancel auto-merge, automated-merge-requests.md:24)

notes: Facts: push options are in every GitLab tier and offering (automated-merge-requests.md:53, DOC S-2d2dlaeq); -o to a server that does not advertise them stops with 'the receiving end does not support push options' before any ref is updated (:55, CODE S-iwjdorgq), so a retry without -o is safe (:56); a bare test remote needs receive.advertisePushOptions=true and a pre-receive hook can record GIT_PUSH_OPTION_* (:43-44, :68). Free has no merged results pipelines, so sync rebases right before the push (:62); auto-merge needs a successful pipeline (:22), and new commits on main cancel it under the fast-forward and semi-linear methods (:24), so git.md names the merge-commit method as optional host setup. The kb has no push options for GitHub pull requests; on a GitHub integration remote sync takes the fallback, and auto-merge there needs a branch protection rule (github-branch-rules-and-auto-merge.md:32). Whether GitLab's auto-merge reads a branch pipeline is open (TK-yoyjegdq); if it does not, the merge request waits visibly and never merges untested. From the push that lands this story, sync sends the sprint's remaining code items as merge requests: ST-niikw55v “Sprint landing and done follow the lanes” comes next for that reason.
